  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

## Summary

I implemented telephone normalization on owner creation.

**The problem:** The `POST /api/owners` request body is validated by Bean Validation (`@Valid`) against the OpenAPI-generated `OwnerFieldsDto` *before* the controller runs. That DTO carried `pattern: '^[0-9]*$'` for `telephone`, so an input like `(04) 1234-5678` was rejected with 400 before any normalization could happen.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Removed the digits-only `pattern` from the `telephone` field (keeping `minLength: 1` / `maxLength: 20`) so raw phone strings containing separators reach the controller. The generated DTO is rebuilt from this spec at compile time.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — After the existing required-field check, normalize the telephone by stripping every non-digit (`replaceAll("\\D", "")`), require exactly 10 digits (otherwise throw `InvalidOwnerFieldsException(List.of("telephone"))` → 400), and store the normalized 10-digit value on the owner before saving.

**How the tests map to the behavior:**
- `coreStripsToTenDigits`: `(04) 1234-5678` → stored/returned as `0412345678`. ✅
- `errorRejectsTooFewDigits`: `12345` → 5 digits ≠ 10 → 400. ✅
- `errorRejectsBlankTelephone`: `"   "` → caught by the existing blank check → 400. ✅
- `functionalityAcceptsCompleteOwner`: valid 10-digit phone passes unchanged. ✅

The existing `Owner` entity constraints (`@Pattern("^[0-9]{10}$")`, `@Digits`) remain satisfied since the stored value is always exactly 10 digits. The create-only scope means `updateOwner` was intentionally left unchanged.
